https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/news/uk-wo.text: Daniel Kinahan is on his way back to Ireland after being extradited from Dubai to face a charge of directing an organised crime group. The 49-year-old was arrested in Dubai this morning after Gardaí travelled to the United Arab Emirates on the Irish Air Corps' €53 million Dassault Falcon 6X on Saturday. The government jet touched down in Dubai on Saturday night before the handover took place today. It then took off from Dubai's Al Maktoum International Airport at 1.19pm local time, or 10.19am Irish time, and is expected to land at Baldonnel Airport in Dublin at around 7.20pm tonight, the Irish Mirror reports. Kinahan is expected to appear before the Special Criminal Court following his return to Ireland. It is the first time the government jet, which was purchased last year, is understood to have been used to transport an alleged criminal back to Ireland. The aircraft, which has the call sign Irl290, is typically used to transport the Taoiseach and government ministers around the world. It has also been used to transport members of the Army Ranger Wing and to assist with emergency operations. In previous operations, an Irish Air Corps Airbus C295 was used to bring Gerry 'The Monk' Hutch and Sean McGovern back to Ireland. The government jet is understood to have been chosen because it can make the journey from Dubai without requiring a stop. A source said: "This is ultimately about getting Kinahan to Ireland as quickly and as securely as possible - both for him and the Gardaí with him." A major security operation is expected to be in place for Kinahan's return, involving the Defence Forces, Irish Prison Service and multiple Garda units. Several road closures are also expected as Gardaí prepare to transfer him to the Special Criminal Court. Kinahan is expected to be formally charged in connection with allegations that he directed an organised crime group. It is understood the prosecution case will relate to alleged activity during the Kinahan-Hutch feud, which began in 2015. The feud has been linked to a number of killings and attempted killings in Ireland and abroad. Kinahan is expected to be brought before the Special Criminal Court for a brief hearing following his arrival. Three judges of the court are expected to sit for the hearing, where evidence relating to his arrest and charge will be heard. Kinahan will be entitled to legal representation and to be present during the proceedings. He is then expected to be remanded in custody and transferred to the care of the Irish Prison Service. The case against Kinahan is understood to centre on allegations that he directed the Kinahan organised crime group during the period of the feud. It is also understood to include allegations relating to an alleged attempt to target Hutch associate James 'Mago' Gately between 2015 and 2017, as well as an alleged plot targeting Gerry Hutch in Lanzarote in December 2015. The allegations have not been tested at trial and Kinahan has not been convicted of the offences. Gardaí are understood to have gathered evidence from encrypted communications recovered during investigations into the organised crime group. Similar encrypted communications were presented during the trial of Kinahan associate Sean McGovern. McGovern was convicted of directing an organised crime group and was jailed for 24 years over his role in the murder of Noel 'Duck Egg' Kirwan and the targeting of Gately. During that case, the Special Criminal Court heard evidence about encrypted messages exchanged between members and associates of the organisation. Gardaí alleged that a number of encrypted usernames, including 'Bon Neww', 'Bon4' and 'Cap', were linked to Kinahan. The court previously heard allegations that messages sent from accounts believed by Gardaí to be linked to Kinahan contained instructions concerning Gately. READ MORE: Family of tragic Minnie Merriman 'left with nothing' as they try to 'rebuild life' READ MORE: Fake doctor accused of conning patients out of thousands of pounds at bogus clinics In April 2017, Estonian national Imre Arakas travelled to Ireland and was later arrested by Gardaí at an address in Blakestown Cottages. Officers seized a Blackberry device containing encrypted communications which Gardaí said related to an alleged plot against Gately. The court heard that an Emergency Response Unit officer photographed some of the messages before they were remotely wiped. Prosecutors alleged that communications included discussions about locating Gately and carrying out an attack against him. Those allegations formed part of the evidence heard during McGovern's case and are separate from any findings that may be made in Kinahan's proceedings. Kinahan is now expected to face the Irish courts after years of international efforts to bring him back to Ireland. https://www.budapesttimes.hu/hungary/the.text: The Budapest Times The 1956 echo: Fidesz finds Baka guilty of the wrong verdict The Fidesz and KDNP parliamentary group leader called András Baka, elected head of state on Tuesday, unworthy of the office of President of the Republic, in a post on Facebook. Fidesz and KDNP members of parliament did not attend the election and inauguration of the new head of state in the National Assembly, but instead laid a wreath in Tata, at the memorial plaque of the martyrs of the 1956 revolution, commemorating the victims of the Tata volley. János Bóka, the Fidesz parliamentary group leader, spoke in a video uploaded to Facebook from the event about how, in Hungary, two important consensuses had existed right up until the Tisza government came to power: first, that Hungary is an independent, democratic rule-of-law state, and second, that modern Hungary is the spiritual heir of the 1956 revolution. With the Tisza Party coming to power, both consensuses had collapsed, the group leader stressed, adding that they do not regard András Baka as their President of the Republic. Bence Rétvári, also in a video uploaded to Facebook, stated that András Baka is not worthy of being President of the Republic of Hungary, because he who “did not side with the revolutionaries in Strasbourg” does not embody the unity of the nation. The legal proceedings that led to the Strasbourg ruling mentioned by the politician were initiated following the Supreme Court’s judgment of 8 November 2001. The court sentenced János Korbely, a retired lieutenant colonel who was 72 years old at the time, to five years’ imprisonment in the criminal case concerning the 1956 Tata volley fire, which claimed three lives. According to the established facts, on 26 October 1956, Captain János Korbely led approximately 15 officers armed with submachine guns, light machine guns, and hand grenades to the Tata district police headquarters in order to retake the building from the insurgents; there he ordered fire and fired himself, as a result of which three people were killed and three were wounded. In 2001, the Supreme Court classified János Korbely’s act as a crime against humanity committed through the intentional killing of multiple persons, and imposed its sentence on that basis. In a case brought before the European Court of Human Rights, based in Strasbourg, the judges — among them András Baka, who was at the time Hungary’s member of the court — examined whether the act truly met the definition of a crime against humanity, or whether it was “merely” homicide, which would by then have been statute-barred and therefore unpunishable. In making this assessment, they focused primarily on whether Tamás Kaszás, one of the shot rebels, could be considered in the specific circumstances to be a person who had previously “laid down his weapon” — because if so, his shooting would not constitute simple homicide but rather an imprescriptible crime against humanity. The Strasbourg court did not find it provable that Kaszás had reached for his pistol in order to hand it over. In its judgment delivered on 19 September 2008, the Strasbourg court ruled in favour of János Korbely and declared that a crime against humanity had not been committed, and that the conviction handed down by the Supreme Court in 2001 contradicted Article 7 of the European Convention on Human Rights, which provides that no punishment shall be imposed in the absence of a criminal offence. The Strasbourg court reached its decision by eleven votes to six, with András Baka voting with the majority. Ihor Prokopchuk, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Ukraine to Romania , on the occasion of the 35th anniversary of the restoration of Ukraine’s independence: 24 august 2026 Dear partners and friends of Ukraine in Romania! Dragi parteneri ș i prieteni ai Ucrainei î n Rom â nia! Today marks the 35th anniversary of the restoration of Ukraine’s independence. Thirty-five years ago, the Ukrainian people made a conscious choice: to live in their own free and sovereign state, to determine their own future, to cherish their language, culture, and history. Today we celebrate this anniversary in a reality that was imposed upon Ukraine by an aggressive and revanchist neighbour. This neighbour – the russian federation – is not only an existential threat to Ukraine, but also a grave threat to freedom and democratic way of life of all European nations. For the fifth consecutive year, Ukraine is marking the national holiday amidst the ongoing brutal war of aggression, unleashed by russia. Cities and villages, residential buildings, energy facilities, and other civilian infrastructure are ravaged by daily attacks. Civilians are constantly targeted and terrorised, getting killed and wounded. Today, we salute and pay the highest respect to the Ukrainian soldiers who courageously defend Ukraine’s statehood and independence! We also bow our heads in memory of the Ukrainian defenders – men and women – who sacrificed their lives defending Ukraine. We remember the civilians whose lives were claimed by the russian aggressor. Today, we speak with pride about the resolve, resilience and free spirit of the Ukrainian people! Ukraine has made Russia’s plans of invasion fail. Ukraine continues to fight. Ukraine continues to work, recover, develop, and build its European future. Ukraine aspires for peace. A comprehensive, just and lasting peace based on the principles of the UN Charter and respect for Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, one that guarantees security and prevents repetition of russia’s aggression. Ukraine is steadily progressing, by implementing extensive reforms, towards full membership in the European Union and NATO. This is not just a foreign policy objective. It is a civilizational choice made by the Ukrainian people – a choice for freedom, democracy, the rule of law, security, and a European future. The choice which is now defended by Ukrainians with the highest human sacrifice. 2026 has already become a landmark year for Ukrainian-Romanian bilateral partnership. In March, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy paid an official visit to Bucharest and, together with President Nicușor Dan signed a Joint Declaration on establishing a strategic partnership between Ukraine and Romania. This was an important historical decision, which set a solid framework for strengthening close practical cooperation across various fields. For Ukraine, Romania is a key partner in the spheres of security, energy, transport and infrastructure, regional development, European integration. We highly value Romania’s consistent support for Ukraine and its European membership path. Profit de această ocazie pentru a-mi exprima recunoștința deosebită față de statul român și față de poporul român – din toate categoriile sociale – pentru solidaritatea cu Ucraina, pentru sprijinul acordat ucrainenilor care și-au găsit adăpost în România, precum și pentru asistența umanitară, energetică și de altă natură oferită țării mele. Dear friends of Ukraine, Ukraine is preparing for another challenging winter. The aggressor state is escalating the intensity of strikes on energy and critical infrastructure as a tool of terror. Therefore, preparations of the energy sector for winter, the strengthening of Ukraine’s air defenses, and energy resilience will be of crucial importance. We are counting on the steadfast support of our international partners, including Romania. I appeal to all to provide needed assistance to Ukraine in a form you will find possible. In closing, let me underscore the historic significance of maintaining unity and common purpose around multidimensional support for Ukraine as means to defeat the revanchist neoimperial ambitions of russia on the European continent. Skip next section Berlin officially withdraws Olympics bid 09/24/2026 September 24, 2026 Berlin officially withdraws Olympics bid Timothy Jones The Olympic rings, seen here in Paris, won't be headed to Berlin Image: Michel Euler/AP/dpa/picture alliance Berlin has confirmed reports that it is withdrawing its bid to host the Summer Olympics and Paralympics. The decision means that only Munich and the western Rhine/Ruhr region are still in the running as potential hosts, with Hamburg having pulled out in May after failing to win support at a referendum. The withdrawal comes after the socialist Left Party's victory in Berlin's elections on Sunday. The party's lead candidate and potential mayor, Elif Eralp, said she did not support Berlin's bid. The current mayor, Kai Wegner of the conservative Christian Democrats (CDU), told reporters: "Today is a sad day for Berlin, because the Olympic and Paralympic Games would have been a tremendous opportunity." "When Ms. Eralp stated that the bid was effectively off the table ... the leading sports associations made it clear: We cannot give you our approval under these circumstances," he said, adding: "I deeply regret this." Kaweh Niroomand, the volleyball manager who led the Berlin bid, said, "We simply could not offer the political stability required." On Saturday, the German Olympic Committee (DOSB) is to choose a preferred region as part of a bid to the International Olympic Committee to host one of the 2036, 2040 and 2044 Summer Games. The Summer Olympics have been held twice on German soil. Berlin hosted the Games in 1936 in then Nazi-ruled Germany and Munich, then as part of West Germany, was the site of the 1972 Games. https://p.dw.com/p/5NCII Skip next section IN DEPTH: Top economic think tanks raise 2026 GDP growth forecasts 09/24/2026 September 24, 2026 IN DEPTH: Top economic think tanks raise 2026 GDP growth forecasts Jon Shelton Economic experts predicted on Thursday that German GDP will double to 1.3% this year. You can read more about their forecasts for Germany's economic future in the next few years in this article: Germany: Economic institutes double growth forecast for 2026 https://p.dw.com/p/5NCFy Skip next section Planned intelligence reforms trigger heated Bundestag debate 09/24/2026 September 24, 2026 Planned intelligence reforms trigger heated Bundestag debate Timothy Jones Intelligence agencies, including the BfV, whose headquarters are pictured here, could receive more powers Image: Christoph Hardt/Panama Pictures/picture alliance The German parliament has held its first debate on government plans to give intelligence agencies more power as national security is threatened by new dangers at home and from abroad. Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt told parliamentarians that the planned reforms would turn Germany's intelligence agencies — the BND (Bundesnachrichtendienst) , in charge of international intelligence, and the BfV (Bundesamt für Verfassungschutz) , responsible for domestic intelligence — into "true secret services." He said the agencies would no longer just gather information on threats but be equipped to provide "real defense against dangers, attacks and terror." Under the plans, the agencies would receive more power to collect, save and automatically evaluate data, as well as permission to react to sabotage or hacking attacks with counterattacks. Intelligence reforms under fire Various parliamentarians voiced concerns about the reform's implications in what was sometimes a heated discussion. Konstantin von Notz from the Green Party said he recognized the need to "update" the powers of the agencies in view of the growing threat from Russia. But, he said, "the excessive plans for domestic intelligence activities" needed to be trimmed or the the reforms would not survive an appeal to the Constitutional Court . He said the government needed to take the interests of people professionally entrusted with confidential information much more into consideration, especially psychotherapists. Clara Bünger of the socialist Left Party accused the government of breaking down the distinction between intelligence agencies and the police that had been a lesson learned "from the crimes of the German fascists." The far-right politician Gottfried Curio from the Alternative for Germany (AfD) party was strongest in his criticism, saying the government wanted to create a " Stasi 2.0," a reference to the secret service in former communist East Germany. The reforms would bring about "more than a total surveillance state," he said. https://p.dw.com/p/5NCF7 Skip next section Bundestag set for organ donation debate 09/24/2026 September 24, 2026 Bundestag set for organ donation debate Timothy Jones The Bundestag will discuss two separate cross-party proposals on Thursday to increase the number of human organs donated for often life-saving transplant operations. One proposal upholds Germany's current system, under which people who wish to donate organs must actively give permission. Advocates of the proposal say that the shortfall of donated organs can be remedied by campaigns calling on adults to take part and making it easier to register the desire to donate. The other proposal calls for an opt-out scheme under which organs can be removed postmortem from anyone who has not expressly rejected being an organ donor. Backers of this proposal say that although surveys show that most people in Germany are willing to donate their organs, very few actually document this wish. They also cite statistics showing that countries with opt-out schemes have more donations, with Germany lagging behind in international comparisons. Altogether 254 of the 630 members of the Bundestag have signed on to the opt-out scheme, and 58 have backed the first proposal to maintain the current national system. The Bundestag last voted on the issue in 2020, with a majority supporting the opt-in model, even though an opt-out proposal had more signees then, too. France, Spain and the Netherlands are examples of European countries that have opt-out models in place. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c61w.text: Image source, Embassy of India in Israel Image caption, The Indian government has praised captain Smit Machchhar for his "immense courage" during the attack By Ella Kipling Published 3 October 2026, 08:40 BST Updated 1 hour ago The co-pilot who attempted to take control of a Flydubai plane travelling to Israel attacked the pilot with a crash axe, the United Arab Emirates prosecutor general has said. The flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv carrying more than 170 people plunged 17,000ft (5,200m) two and a half hours into its journey, before passengers managed to overpower the attacker and successfully take control of the plane. Capt Smit Machchhar said he was lying on the floor injured when he realised the plane was sinking and he had to act, explaining: "I told myself to go for one last push to open the door from inside", which allowed the passengers in. Two reserve pilots then landed the plane safely in Saudi Arabia. A crash axe is usually kept âin the cockpit in case of emergencies. The UAE attorney general told state media that investigations were ongoing to determine the full circumstances and motives of the incident. The co-pilot who launched the attack was an Omani national, according to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Multiple media outlets including Reuters, CNN and The New York Times have named him as Hamam al-Hammami. There has been no official confirmation of this. While working at another airline, Oman Air, US media reported that Al-Hammami was removed from flight training because of concerns over his radical views, and was given another role at Oman's national airline. He completed a three-year distance-learning course at Buckinghamshire New University in the UK and graduated with a degree in aviation management in 2023, the university said. It added he did not take any pilot training at the school. Speaking to Fox News, Netanyahu said that after the attacker was subdued on the flight, he called out to the crew "Kill me, kill me!" The Israeli prime minister added: "So, it's clear that he was suicidalâ¦ It looks very likely that he was going to down the plane." He also said the attacker "underwent Islamist radical indoctrination". The UAE has begun investigating whether the "incident was linked to any terrorist activity or purpose", according to the country's state news agency. Machchhar, who was stabbed in the attack, was taken to a nearby hospital before being airlifted to Abu Dhabi, where he is reported to be in a stable condition. The pilot, who is from India, was in "good health and recovering well", the Indian embassy in the UAE said on Thursday. "I am confident that the recovery will be there and I will become fit and healthy again," Machchhar said. About two and half hours after the plane took off from Dubai International Airport it begun to plunge sharply. The plane signalled a "general emergency" code, squawk 7700, before switching to squawk 7500, a code reporting "unlawful interference", or hijacking. In an interview with the BBC, one passenger described the moment he realised that something was wrong. Almog Itali said: "Suddenly the aeroplane started to, like a rollercoaster, to drop down [with] a massive G-force. It was falling down for 20 or 30 seconds, rapidly, and then balanced, and then started once again to fall down." People then began to rush to the cockpit, he said. Israeli President Isaac Herzog said on Thursday that the alarm was raised onboard by an Israeli woman, Tali Manes, who heard a commotion coming from the cockpit. Her husband, Zvika, along with three other men - Yaniv Hayun, Dr Shota Musayev and Asaf Rajuan - entered the cockpit after Capt Machchhar managed to open the door despite his injuries. Hayun said, in a video released by the prime minister's office, that the attacker was "trying to destroy the instruments in order to disable the plane". Hayun then described putting the attacker in a chokehold and pulling him outside the cockpit before other passengers helped to pin him down. He added that he "pulled the controls" of the plane. "The plane started to level out, a bit more, and then [another] pilot told me he was taking control from there," he said. In an interview with CNN on Wednesday evening, Netanyahu said the stabbed pilot, passengers and second crew had "managed to prevent a 9/11 disaster".
